title: A Good Mend
hook: Turn a tear into the most beautiful part of a garment: choose a continuous stitch that secures the cloth around a keepsake emblem, then pull it tight.
audience: Players who enjoy calm spatial puzzles, tactile restoration and making a personal object look better.
core_loop: Inspect a tear and two requirements; preview a stitch route; sew and tighten; see what is secured; undo or keep the repair in a gallery; try a new commission.
working_title_note: Working name; no name or trademark clearance established.
evidence_limits: Desk research only. No competitor hands-on session, own playable build, target-player interview, fun validation or purchase-intent measurement. Historical topic growth is distinct from a verified current trend phase.
commercial_hypothesis: Offline premium Windows microgame. USD 3.99-5.99 is an initial price question. Owner ceiling USD 9.99 is conditional on genre/price evidence and a worthwhile few-day product; no basis to charge the ceiling yet.

cash_assumptions.note: Planning inputs only, no spending authorized. Existing machine/tools assumed; subscription/compute costs not measured. Steam fee and any applicable store tax separate from optional assets.

calendar_note: Build estimates include the prototype, final-direction art/audio, finite content, save/settings, packaged Windows QA and draft store media. Steam onboarding/review/waiting and recruitment are separate; no launch date committed.
support_estimate: Reserve 1–2 owner hours around launch for triage/review, with agent implementation as needed; actual demand and defect burden unknown.

decision_history.reason: Research recommendation only; owner has not selected a game or authorized a prototype.

Retained among eight as a tightly bounded tactile-puzzle alternative. Its earlier first-place ranking was superseded by the wider genre/price comparison. Direct low-price PC sewing response is weak; the interaction remains unplayed.

score_notes.demand: Reassessed under the USD 9.99 ceiling: stitch. is close but not Steam unit evidence; Calico is USD 19.99 and above ceiling. Sewing Stuff has only 15 Steam-purchase reviews. Adjacent tactile games support the format, not our repair demand.
score_notes.distinctiveness: Chosen functional/decorative tear repair differs from numbered embroidery regions and timed point tracing, but neither sewing nor thread puzzles are novel by themselves.
score_notes.fun_potential: Planning a repair and seeing it tighten is untested; it may collapse to tracing.
score_notes.scope_fit: 4–6-day estimate is conditional on a convincing fake-cloth reveal and fast authored repairs. No real cloth simulation.
score_notes.distribution: A torn-to-repaired before/after has a natural connection to visible-mending content. No creator interest or conversion measured.

inspiration.topic: Visible mending, sashiko and clothing upcycling
inspiration.connection: The player performs the source activity: repairing cloth while making the repair expressive.
inspiration.why_phase_unverified: Pinterest reports May-to-May growth; Etsy offers adjacent earlier evidence. No monthly series proving September acceleration or a future peak.
inspiration.evergreen_promise: Spatial planning, the transformation from damaged to repaired, and collecting personally chosen patterns remain meaningful after fashion attention changes.
inspiration.searchable_name: Optional. Prefer an appealing title; visible mending and stitching can appear naturally in truthful descriptions.

evidence.claim: Pinterest reports sashiko ideas +1,509%, darning stitch +91% and refashion clothes upcycling +230%; global text searches, May 2026 versus May 2025. Report published August 25, 2026. This is historical growth, not a measured September slope.
evidence.access_note: Direct public HTML verified after web-tool regional redirect.

evidence.claim: Etsy describes interest in stitched craft and reports beginner needlepoint kits +175%. Data as of February 10, 2026 compares the preceding three months with a year earlier, using US signed-in normalized searches. This is adjacent corroboration, not exact mending-game demand.
The developer presents numbered embroidery puzzles and free stitching. This establishes a close tactile reference; our functional tear repair is a proposed difference.
Apple's June 5, 2023 developer interview describes the material and accessibility work behind stitch.; sensory quality is part of the production burden.

Sewing Stuff already sells restoring objects through point connections with time pressure. Our API snapshot has 15 all-language Steam-purchase reviews, 11 positive. The small response is counterevidence to assuming sewing alone attracts buyers.

The paid fabric-pattern board game is an adjacent audience reference, with 405 consistently filtered reviews, 379 positive, in the saved API snapshot. It has a broader scope than our proposed product.

A Tiny Sticker Tale: USD 9.99 regular/current, 471 all-language Steam-purchase reviews, 97.2% positive in this run. Adjacent tactile puzzle/adventure, not direct repair demand or disclosed unit sales.

prototype_envelope.scope: One cloth surface, three tears, one stitch rule, preview, undo and one finished-direction tightening reveal.

production_envelope.scope: One 2D work surface, three reusable cloth sets, up to 18 small repair cards, one core stitch rule and at most two modifiers, completion gallery and local save.
production_envelope.owner_note: Agent branch estimated 1.5–2 hours for play/presentation review; producer allows 3–5 including repeat feedback and store-material review. Recruitment/account-verification time remains unknown.

risks: Reported interest includes a desire for physical, screen-free hobbies; a PC game may not satisfy that audience.
Stitches may look decorative without providing a meaningful decision.
Convincing material feedback and clear failure explanation could exceed the estimate.
18 repair cards is a cap, not proof of sufficient value; content authorship must be tested.
Current trend stage, organic reach, willingness to pay and actual fun remain unverified.
next_test: If chosen, use the one-day prototype for a 15-minute owner playtest, followed by four other target players when available. Continue if 4/5 can predict what a stitch secures without coaching and 3/5 voluntarily start another repair. Require at least one deliberate choice between a functional and decorative route. Hold if two tuning passes still yield obvious tracing or confusing repairs. These are directional criteria, not statistical validation.
decision_reason: Retained among eight as a tightly bounded tactile-puzzle alternative. Its earlier first-place ranking was superseded by the wider genre/price comparison. Direct low-price PC sewing response is weak; the interaction remains unplayed.
